sents.t: Document 1: E-mail
To: All Registered Exhibitors From: Olivia Grant, Event Coordinator Subject: Important Information about the Expo
Dear Exhibitors,
Thank you for registering for the Harbor City Business Expo, which will take place at the Seaside Convention Center from April 15 to April 17.
This year, we are expecting more than 8,000 attendees and approximately 250 exhibitors from over twenty countries.
That would make it the largest event in the expo's twelve-year history.
To help everything run smoothly, please read the following information carefully.
First, all exhibitors are required to set up their booths on April 14 between 1:00 P.M. and 7:00 P.M.
Setup will not be permitted on the morning of April 15, because the doors open to the public at 9:00 A.M.
If you are unable to arrive on April 14, please contact me as soon as possible so that we can make alternative arrangements.
Second, each booth comes with one table, two chairs, and access to a standard electrical outlet.
Additional furniture and equipment, such as display screens and extra lighting, can be rented through our online order form.
Orders placed before March 25 will receive a 15 percent discount.
After that date, standard prices will apply, and we cannot guarantee that all items will be available.
Third, please note that the parking garage next to the convention center will be under construction during the event.
Exhibitors may park in the east lot free of charge by showing their exhibitor badge at the entrance.
However, space is limited, so we strongly encourage you to use public transportation whenever possible.
The convention center is located just a five-minute walk from Harbor Station.
Fourth, exhibitor badges can be picked up at the registration desk in the main lobby from 12:00 P.M. on April 14.
Each company will receive up to four badges.
If you need more, you can purchase them for $20 each.
Please make sure that your staff members wear their badges at all times while they are in the building.
Free wireless Internet access is available throughout the convention center, but the connection may become slow when the halls are crowded.
If your booth depends on a reliable connection, for example for product demonstrations, we recommend ordering a wired connection in advance.
Finally, I would like to remind everyone about our new rule regarding giveaways.
Last year, one exhibitor handed out 3,000 balloons shaped like their company logo.
The balloons were very popular, but about half of them ended up stuck to the ceiling of the main hall, and it took our maintenance staff two full days to remove them.
Therefore, balloons are no longer allowed at the expo.
Small items such as pens, notebooks, and tote bags are still welcome.
A detailed schedule of the expo, including seminars and networking events, is attached to this e-mail.
If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact me by phone at 555-0193 or by replying to this e-mail.
We look forward to seeing you in April.
Best regards, Olivia Grant
Document 2: Expo Schedule
Harbor City Business Expo Schedule of Events
Day 1, Wednesday, April 15
9:00 A.M.: Doors open to the public.
10:00 A.M.: Opening speech by Mayor Rachel Dunn in the Main Hall.
11:00 A.M.: Seminar: "Growing Your Small Business Through Social Media," presented by Kevin Osei, marketing director at Brightpath Media.
2:00 P.M.: Seminar: "Reducing Shipping Costs for Online Stores," presented by Hannah Weiss, founder of ParcelWise.
6:00 P.M.: Welcome reception for exhibitors at the Seaside Hotel ballroom. Light refreshments will be served.
Day 2, Thursday, April 16
9:00 A.M.: Doors open.
10:30 A.M.: Keynote speech: "The Future of Remote Work," presented by Dr. Samuel Price, author of the best-selling book Working from Anywhere.
1:00 P.M.: Panel discussion: "Finding and Keeping Talented Employees," featuring four human resources managers from local companies.
3:30 P.M.: Workshop: "Writing a Business Plan That Investors Will Read," led by Maria Santos of Coastline Bank. Advance registration required; limited to 40 participants.
7:00 P.M.: Networking dinner at Harbor View Restaurant. Tickets: $45 per person.
Day 3, Friday, April 17
9:00 A.M.: Doors open.
11:00 A.M.: Seminar: "Protecting Your Company from Online Fraud," presented by Victor Lang, security consultant.
2:00 P.M.: Award ceremony for the Best Booth Design.
4:00 P.M.: The expo closes. Exhibitors must remove all materials from their booths by 8:00 P.M.
Please note that all seminars are held in Room B unless otherwise stated.
The schedule is subject to change without notice.
Document 3: E-mail
To: Olivia Grant From: Daniel Cho Subject: Setup and Workshop Date: April 8
Dear Ms. Grant,
My name is Daniel Cho, and I am the sales manager at Greenhill Tea Company, one of the exhibitors at this year's expo.
I am writing regarding two matters.
First, I am afraid that our team will not be able to set up our booth on April 14 as scheduled.
Our flight from Vancouver was canceled due to a mechanical problem, and the earliest flight we could book arrives at 11:30 P.M. that night.
I understand that setup is not allowed on the morning of the first day.
Would it be possible for a member of your staff to let us in late at night on April 14, or very early on April 15?
Our booth is quite simple, so it should take no more than an hour to set up.
To be honest, the most difficult part is inflating our two-meter teapot, which we use to attract visitors.
Please don't worry; it is not a balloon, and it will not end up on your ceiling.
Second, I would like to register two of my staff members for the business plan workshop on April 16.
I tried to sign up online, but the registration page said that the session was full.
If anyone cancels, could you please put us on the waiting list?
Both of them joined our company this year and are responsible for developing our new business plan for the European market.
I believe the workshop would be extremely useful for them.
They would also be happy to attend any other session on the same topic if one is available.
Also, I placed an order for a display screen on March 28, but I have not yet received a confirmation.
Could you check whether the order was processed correctly?
Thank you for your help, and I apologize for any inconvenience this may cause.
Sincerely, Daniel Cho
Document 4: E-mail
To: Daniel Cho From: Olivia Grant Subject: RE: Setup and Workshop Date: April 9
Dear Mr. Cho,
Thank you for letting me know about your situation, and I am sorry to hear about your flight.
I have spoken with our security team, and a guard will be available to let you into the building at 6:30 A.M. on April 15.
Please note, however, that your booth must be completely ready by 8:45 A.M., when we do our final safety check.
Please enter through the loading dock on the north side of the building, not through the main entrance.
Our staff will also help you carry your materials from the dock to your booth using carts.
Since you will be arriving so late the night before, I have also asked the Seaside Hotel to hold your team's reservation even if you check in after midnight.
Regarding the workshop, I have some good news.
Because so many people were interested, Ms. Santos has kindly agreed to hold a second session on Friday, April 17, at 1:00 P.M. in Room C.
I have already registered your two staff members for that session.
If they would prefer to stay on the waiting list for the Thursday session instead, just let me know.
As for your equipment order, it was processed on March 29, and the screen will be delivered to your booth before the doors open.
I checked our records and found that the confirmation e-mail had been sent to an incorrect address because of a typing error on our part.
I sincerely apologize for this mistake.
Please also note that because the order was placed after the deadline, the discount could not be applied.
Finally, a two-meter teapot sounds wonderful.
You might want to consider entering the Best Booth Design award.
Last year's winner was a booth shaped like a giant sandwich, so the judges clearly appreciate creative ideas.
Best regards, Olivia Grant
Document 5: Article
Harbor City Expo Breaks Attendance Record
By Thomas Reed, Harbor City Times, April 18
The twelfth annual Harbor City Business Expo ended yesterday with a record number of visitors.
According to the organizers, about 9,300 people attended the three-day event, far more than the 8,000 they had originally expected.
"We were surprised by the turnout," said event coordinator Olivia Grant.
"On the second day, the line at the entrance stretched all the way to Harbor Station."
The most popular session was Dr. Samuel Price's keynote speech on remote work.
The Main Hall was so crowded that the organizers had to set up extra screens in the lobby so that more people could watch.
Dr. Price told the audience that he had written most of his latest book in coffee shops in eleven different countries.
"The only place I could not work," he joked, "was my own office."
Small business owners also praised the workshop on writing business plans.
Because of high demand, a second session was added on the final day, and both sessions were fully booked.
Maria Santos of Coastline Bank, who led the workshop, said she was pleased to see so many young entrepreneurs.
"Many of them have excellent ideas," she said. "They simply need to explain them more clearly."
Not every part of the event went smoothly, however.
Because the parking garage next to the convention center was closed for construction, many visitors had trouble finding a place to park.
Some exhibitors also complained that the wireless Internet was too slow to show videos of their products.
Ms. Grant said that the organizers would take these comments into account when planning next year's event.
Overall, however, most participants described the expo as a great success.
Kevin Osei, who gave a seminar on the first day, said he had collected more than 200 business cards.
"I will be busy answering e-mails for the next month," he said with a smile.
The Best Booth Design award went to Greenhill Tea Company, a Vancouver-based business that sells organic tea online and in more than 60 stores.
Its booth featured a two-meter teapot that visitors could actually walk inside.
"We almost didn't make it," said sales manager Daniel Cho, who explained that his team had finished setting up only minutes before the doors opened on the first day.
The organizers have already announced that next year's expo will be held at a larger venue, the newly built Harbor City Arena, which can hold up to 15,000 visitors.
The arena is located right next to Harbor Station and has its own parking garage with 3,000 spaces.
Registration for exhibitors will begin in October.
Ms. Grant added that balloons will still not be allowed.
